hypothesis: The 8-neighbour outer-totalistic 2D cellular automaton 'a cell becomes black when exactly three of its eight neighbours are black, otherwise it is unchanged' (NKS code 174826, Life-like notation B3/S012345678), started from a row of eleven black cells, keeps growing for 1000 steps while the normalised outline of the whole pattern keeps changing on the scale of the pattern itself and never settles to a simple geometric form (circle, square, diamond or octagon), whereas simple growth rules settle to a fixed simple outline.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Run the rule for T = 1000 steps from a row of 11 black cells. Let rho_t(theta) be the outer radius of the occupied set from the pattern centroid in 360 angular bins, normalised by its mean, and D(t1,t2) the mean absolute difference between rho_t1 and rho_t2. PASS (supports) if all three hold: (a) growth continues: mean radius R(1000) >= 1.5 * R(500) and the population is larger at step 1000 than at step 500; (b) the outline keeps changing: D(500,1000) >= 0.05 and D(750,1000) >= 0.03, while both control rules (8-neighbour 'black if any neighbour black', which grows a square, and 4-neighbour 'black if any neighbour black', which grows a diamond) give D(500,1000) <= 0.02; (c) the outline at step 1000 is not a simple form: the minimum over the reference family {circle, axis-aligned square, 45-degree square, regular octagon at 0 and 22.5 degrees} of the mean absolute difference between rho_1000 and the reference profile is >= 0.05, while for each control rule the same minimum is <= 0.03.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. FAIL (refutes) if growth stops (population unchanged over steps 900-1000) or if the outline converges to a simple form: D(500,1000) < 0.02 and the minimum simple-shape distance at step 1000 is < 0.03. Any other combination is 'mixed' (e.g. shape still changing but growth slowing, or controls not behaving as expected, which would mean the descriptor is not discriminating).
interpretation: Wolfram's claim (pp. 176, 181) is existential: this one rule from this one seed produces an overall shape that 'seems continually to go on changing, with no simple overall form'. 'Overall shape' is mapped to the normalised angular outer-radius profile of the occupied set, so interior texture is ignored; 'no simple form' is mapped to distance from a small pre-declared family of simple convex shapes and to non-convergence of the outline between steps 500, 750 and 1000. 'Continually' can only be bounded by the run length; a finite run cannot exclude eventual regularity. Code 175850 (the '3 or 5 of 8' rule from p. 177, row of 7), which the book says is rough on small scales but smooth on large scales, is run as an additional comparison but is not part of the criterion.

datasets.name: Enumerated evolution of the 2D outer-totalistic 8-neighbour cellular automaton, NKS code 174826 (birth on exactly 3 black neighbours, otherwise unchanged), generated by analysis.py
datasets.license: generated by this test; rule definition from NKS p. 176

generator.program_family: 2D outer-totalistic cellular automata on the Moore (8-cell) neighbourhood; NKS 9-neighbour outer-totalistic code: bit 2k = new colour of a white cell with k black neighbours, bit 2k+1 = new colour of a black cell with k black neighbours
controls: 8-neighbour 'black if at least one neighbour black' (square growth)
4-neighbour von Neumann 'black if at least one neighbour black' (diamond growth)
generator.initial_condition: horizontal row of 11 black cells on an otherwise white infinite plane (controls: same seed; code 175850: row of 7 as in the book)
generator.grid: unbounded; array grown dynamically so the boundary never touches the edge

datasets.role: the computational object the claim is about
